title: Tenant soft-accounting and forecast-driven priming to prevent GPU queue collapse
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary:
During the 2026-02-21 capacity event the hosted API experienced rapid tenant fanout which caused persistent GPU occupancy spikes and a cascading queue buildup across multiple pools. Unlike previous incidents, this one surfaced two correlated failure modes: (1) short-term transient bursts from bursty tenants that repeatedly requeued after soft rejects, and (2) slow-response autoscaler decisions because of relying solely on pod counts rather than instantaneous GPU occupancy and active KV-cache population.

Root cause (short):
- Tenant-level admission used a coarse credit window that allowed repeated retries to amplify queue pressure.
- Autoscaler undershot because our scaling signals used pod-level CPU/memory and not occupancy-adjusted token rates.
- Prefix/KV cache coldness increased per-request time and reduced effective throughput during initial scaling.

What we did during the incident (mitigations):
- Rapidly enforced a temporary hard backoff per-tenant (5s jittered) to stop repeated requeues.
- Manually increased autoscaler target counts for two affected pools to buy time for safe draining.
- Enabled emergency cross-pool fallback to move low-priority traffic to best-effort pools.
These actions stabilized tail latency within 30 minutes but did not address root causes.

Proposal (long-term):
We propose a combined system of: 1) tenant soft-accounting (per-tenant credit buckets with decay and emergency borrow), 2) forecast-driven priming (using a short-window workload fingerprint to prewarm KV cache and warm-up kernels in selected replicas), and 3) occupancy-aware autoscaling (occupancy and active-token-rate metrics drive scale decisions alongside pods).

Details: 
- Tenant soft-accounting: each tenant receives credits proportional to recent steady-state usage. Credits decay (exponential with configurable half-life) and allow brief bursts. When credits dip below a threshold the tenant receives graded degradation responses (slow-path, truncated responses, 429 with Retry-After) instead of immediate hard eviction. Borrowing is allowed up to a safety cap; borrow decays at an elevated rate. This reduces retry amplification compared to current hard tries.
- Forecast-driven priming: when a tenant's fingerprint (small hash of request meta + prompt length distribution) suggests an imminent burst, the system will prime: (a) prefetch common KV prefixes into a warm cache slice, (b) spin up 1-2 warm replicas with warmed kernels and cache, (c) bias routing to replicas with warm caches. Forecast window is short (30s–3min) and uses exponentially-weighted average of recent arrival rates.
- Occupancy-aware autoscaler: new metrics (GPU_occupancy_95, active_token_rate_p50) will join the autoscaler decision matrix. We will add a short-timescale ramp policy: fast horizontal scaling for sustained occupancy > 75% for 30s, with a cooldown to avoid oscillation. Combine with a soft-prewarm quota so new replicas start with warm kernels if selected for priming.

Telemetry & dashboards:
- New metrics to add: tenant_credit_balance, tenant_borrow_level, pool_occupancy_95, active_token_rate, pool_cache_warm_pct, forecast_priming_trigger_rate.
- Dashboard: "Pool Health — Occupancy & Credit" with tenant-level drilldowns, and a heatmap of forecast triggers vs. actual burst arrivals.

Acceptance criteria / rollout plan: 
- Stage 1 (canary, 2 weeks): implement tenant soft-accounting in the admission service; expose tenant_credit_balance metric; soft-blocking enabled for 5% of traffic (internal tenants). Success if queued requests and retry amplification reduced by >=40% in canary.
- Stage 2 (integration, 3 weeks): add occupancy metrics to autoscaler and implement short-timescale ramp; run on staging and then 10% of production traffic. Verify stable scaling without oscillation for 24h load tests.
- Stage 3 (opt-in priming, 2 weeks): enable forecast-driven priming for a subset of high-variance tenants; evaluate cache hit uplift and latency improvement.
- Final (global rollout): enable tenant soft-accounting globally; occupancy autoscaler becomes default; priming enabled for top 25% volatile tenants.

Test plan:
- Synthetic tenant fanout generator to reproduce repeated retry amplification patterns (open-source harness linked below).
- Chaos test: random delayed autoscaler responses to validate safety nets and fallback routing.
- Load tests: 72-hour soak with scheduled bursts to validate cooldown prevents oscillation.

Artifacts & links:
- Internal design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CR/tenant-soft-accounting-and-priming
- Simulation harness (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/capacity-sim/compare/ENG-404321
- Draft PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/8124 (admission changes), https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/409 (occupancy signals)

Risks & mitigations: 
- Oscillation risk: can occur if priming and autoscaler both trigger aggressively. Mitigation: central coordinator enforces a per-pool priming budget and a minimum stabilization window (60–120s) between scale actions.
- Fairness: soft-accounting must include tenant weight adjustments to prevent small tenants being starved. Mitigation: add weight floor and manual override.
- Complexity and operator burden: add clear runbooks and a "panic button" to flip to legacy hard-throttle behavior.

Outcomes expected: 
- Reduce retry-amplified queue growth by 60–80% for bursty tenants.
- Lower tail latency during scale events by warm-cache priming + occupancy-aware scaling.
- Give platform operators better visibility into tenant-level debt and preemptive priming triggers.

Next immediate steps (this ticket):
- Implement admission-side tenant_credit_balance counter and the decay/borrrow algorithm (ENG-404322).
- Add GPU occupancy 95th percentile to autoscaler metrics and a short-timescale ramp policy (ENG-404323).
- Create forecast priming prototype as spike work (Spike ticket, separate).

Notes: this approach intentionally biases toward soft degradation over immediate eviction to reduce retry amplification and give autoscaler signals time to react. It complements existing prewarm work but is focused on tenant-level economics and short-term forecasting rather than broad pool prewarm schedules.
comments: 2026-03-01 — Liam Chen: Implemented initial tenant_credit_balance counter and exported metrics to telemetry pipeline (PR linked in description). Running unit tests; basic decay function in place. Observed expected behavior in local sim: credits decay ~halflife configured.

2026-03-03 — Maya Thompson (SRE): Verified new metrics appear in dogfood cluster dashboards. Added temporary alert 'tenant-credit-negative-rate' for canary. Enabled soft-block for internal tenants group. Initial canary shows 46% reduction in requeue loops for canary tenants.
2026-03-05 — Product (Noah Singh): Confirmed product acceptance for soft-degrade UX; agreed on standard 429 payload with Retry-After and 'soft_degraded' header to surface to downstream clients.

2026-03-09 — Liam Chen: Autoscaler prototype updated to consume pool_occupancy_95. Ran staging experiment with a synthetic burst and autoscaler responded in ~45s vs ~120s previously. Need to tune cooldown to avoid flip-flop.

2026-03-12 — Ava Patel: Added rollout checklist and scheduled a cross-team review (SRE, Serving, Autoscale, DX) for 2026-03-16. Also flagged requirement for a one-click revert in console for the global rollout.
